DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: <role>: the role the goal names, such as "the developer". <achieves what>: what the role achieves with the deliverable. Give either template or parts, never both: template where the kind's deliverable is one document, and parts where it's a set of files of a known form, such as code or a prompt. <kind>: the kind of deliverable, such as "readme". <ext>: the deliverable's own format, such as "md". example: one deliverable made by the best practice and passed, or a folder of several that differ; optional until one deliverable of the kind passes. <source>: the path, from the best practice's folder, of the deliverable the example is a copy of; optional, where the example is no copy. inputs: each kind whose deliverables a deliverable of this kind is made from, and preconditions: each kind whose deliverables must pass before it's made, each <kind> by the name of its best practice's folder, so that the plan orders each deliverable after what it takes; each list empty where it takes none.

parts.DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: One for each file or piece of a file the deliverable holds, such as a module's interface. <part>: a short id. <what the role needs>: what the role needs of the part, so that the generator makes it to that need. A part made of parts holds them under parts, three deep at most.

intents.DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: One for each way makers of the kind fail the role, as deliverables made without the best practice show and the field's sources name, and one about the whole; in the order the generator thinks them. <section>: a section of the template or a part, as written there, or "the whole". <When>: the moment a role uses it, such as "Reading the goal". <role>: the role that uses it, the one the goal names or one that serves it, such as "the evaluator". <get what>: what that role needs from it there. <so that>: what the role is after in getting it, toward the goal, so that the generator and the evaluator judge by that intent; left out where <get what> is the goal itself.

practices.DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: One for each question, in the questions' order. <name>: the name the field knows the practice by, such as "information hiding". <other name>: each other name it goes by; optional. <must be>: what the deliverable must be for the question's role, in short sentences. <why>: why the role needs it so, what goes wrong for the role otherwise. <where it applies>, and <where it doesn't>, with what to do there instead. <what it costs>: what following it costs. <title> and <url>: each source the practice rests on, by its title and where it lies; secondary true where only a summary of it was read, else left out. <step>: an action whose skipping or order breaks the deliverable; optional. trace: the call that shows the step done, as a guard, such as Lane, holds a step by it in the steps' order and holds the role's end until it comes back. <action>, in the form rn's guard reads: run for a command run, matched whole, read for a file read to its end, or write for a file made. <take>: the command or the file's path, written as the step writes it, a value the role's start gives as `{<name>}`, such as `{deliverable}`, a whole take for a file or one word of a command; for run and write, more than one where any of them shows the step done, and for read, each file the step reads whole.
